newsitem.title: SPAIN: Madrid stocks close flat after another rocky ride.
newsitem.headline: Madrid stocks close flat after another rocky ride.

text.p: Madrid stocks eventually closed flat on Friday after a volatile day's trade which was dominated by Wall Street, dealers said.
Sharp losses in New York yesterday meant the market mainly passed off a Bank of Spain key money rate cut this morning.
The general index rose 0.09 points, 0.02 percent, to 485.20 and the Ibex added 1.40 points, 0.03 percent, to 5,568.05.
Gas Natural outperformed, adding 730 pesetas, or 2.24 percent, after state holding firm SEPI approved the sale of nine percent in Enagas to Gas Natural for 14 billion pesetas.
Repsol, which holds a controlling stake in Gas Natural, ended up 70 pesetas to 5,970.

The Bank of Spain's decision to cut its key rate by 25 basis points to 5.75 percent this morning, as largely anticipated by the market, was well-received, as was lower-than-expected February inflation on Thursday, dealers said.
Inflation fell 0.1 pct from January, up 2.5 pct on the year.
"The rate cut after excellent February inflation data was eclipsed this morning by New York's performance. Wall Street calls the tune," said one dealer.
In the short-term, dealers remain cautious.
